about: Every dataset, package and paper MycoMap Atlas is built on, and every file the pipeline produces. The Sources page and the /api/sources route read this file; tests/testthat/test-sources.R fails when the code calls a package, or the web app depends on one, that is not listed here.

datasets.name: MycoMap validated collections
datasets.license: Record-level data stays on mycomap.org; Atlas publishes 0.1° cells only
datasets.role: Training data: every collection whose name was confirmed by DNA sequencing and validated in a MycoMap project.
datasets.citation: MycoMap.org validated collections, read at the pull recorded in each release.

datasets.name: WorldClim 2.1 bioclimatic variables and elevation
datasets.role: Nineteen climate predictors (1970-2000 normals) and elevation, from which slope and roughness are derived.
datasets.citation: Fick SE, Hijmans RJ (2017) WorldClim 2: new 1-km spatial resolution climate surfaces for global land areas. International Journal of Climatology 37:4302-4315.

datasets.name: SoilGrids 2.0
datasets.role: Topsoil (0-5 cm) pH, organic carbon, total nitrogen, clay, sand and cation exchange capacity.
datasets.citation: Poggio L, de Sousa LM, Batjes NH, et al. (2021) SoilGrids 2.0: producing soil information for the globe with quantified spatial uncertainty. SOIL 7:217-240.

datasets.name: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200
datasets.role: Fractions of tree, shrub, grass, wetland, open-water and built-up cover, aggregated to 30 arc-seconds.
datasets.citation: Zanaga D, Van De Kerchove R, Daems D, et al. (2022) ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200.

datasets.name: USFS FIA BIGMAP 2018 tree species aboveground biomass
datasets.provider: USDA Forest Service, Forest Inventory and Analysis
datasets.role: Host trees in the lower 48: biomass of each tree species at 30 m, read at 250 m and averaged into the share of each host genus, and of conifers, in a cell's trees: the 19 mostly mycorrhizal host genera, and the 10 decay and parasite hosts (maple, ash, elm, juniper, cedar, tulip tree, cherry, sweetgum, sycamore, black locust).
datasets.citation: Wilson BT, Knight JF, McRoberts RE (2018) Harmonic regression of Landsat time series for modeling attributes from national forest inventory data. ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 137:29-46. Data: USDA Forest Service FIA BIGMAP 2018 tree species aboveground biomass.

datasets.name: Canada's National Forest Inventory kNN forest attributes, 2011
datasets.provider: Natural Resources Canada, Canadian Forest Service
datasets.role: Host trees in Canada: percent composition of each tree species at 250 m, summed by genus and averaged into the share of each host genus, and of conifers, among a cell's identified trees (decay and parasite hosts included; tulip tree, sweetgum, sycamore and black locust are not mapped in Canada and are 0 there). Contains information licensed under the Open Government Licence - Canada.
datasets.citation: Beaudoin A, Bernier PY, Guindon L, et al. (2014) Mapping attributes of Canada's forests at moderate resolution through kNN and MODIS imagery. Canadian Journal of Forest Research 44:521-532 (doi:10.1139/cjfr-2013-0401). Data: Canada's National Forest Inventory 2011 kNN forest attributes, doi:10.23687/ec9e2659-1c29-4ddb-87a2-6aced147a990.

datasets.name: US Census cartographic boundary files, states, 1:500,000 (2023)
datasets.role: Where the lower 48 are, so BIGMAP's empty cells can be told from the rest of the continent. Not a predictor.

datasets.name: Natural Earth 5.1.1: admin-1 states and provinces (1:10m), countries and lakes (1:50m)
datasets.role: Which state, province or territory each map cell lies in, for the lists of where a species is likely; and land, lakes and borders under the map pictures. Cut to North America and simplified to about 2 km by tools/build-boundaries.R, kept in inst/boundaries. Not a predictor.

datasets.name: NALCMS Land Cover 2020, 30 m
datasets.provider: Commission for Environmental Cooperation (CCRS, USGS, CONABIO, CONAFOR, INEGI)
datasets.role: Candidate layer: share of each cell under needleleaf, broadleaf and mixed forest, counted from 30 m pixels.
datasets.citation: Commission for Environmental Cooperation (2024) North American Environmental Atlas - Land Cover 2020 30m. NALCMS. Ed. 2.0.

datasets.name: Copernicus Global Land Cover 100 m, collection 3, 2019
datasets.role: Forest type where NALCMS is silent: Hawaii and the Caribbean islands, read from the discrete classification map and split into needleleaf, broadleaf and mixed forest.
datasets.citation: Buchhorn M, Smets B, Bertels L, De Roo B, Lesiv M, Tsendbazar N-E, Herold M, Fritz S (2020) Copernicus Global Land Service: Land Cover 100m: collection 3: epoch 2019: Globe. Zenodo.

datasets.name: AdaptWest ClimateNA 1991-2020 normals, 1 km
datasets.role: Candidate layer: climatic moisture deficit, autumn precipitation and temperature, frost-free period, precipitation as snow and relative humidity.
datasets.citation: AdaptWest Project (2022) Gridded current and projected climate data for North America at 1km resolution, generated using the ClimateNA v7.30 software (Wang T et al. 2022). Wang T, Hamann A, Spittlehouse D, Carroll C (2016) Locally downscaled and spatially customizable climate data for historical and future periods for North America. PLoS One 11:e0156720.

datasets.name: TerraClimate 1991-2020 climatology
datasets.provider: Climatology Lab, University of California Merced
datasets.role: Candidate layer: annual actual evapotranspiration and mean vapour pressure deficit.
datasets.citation: Abatzoglou JT, Dobrowski SZ, Parks SA, Hegewisch KC (2018) TerraClimate, a high-resolution global dataset of monthly climate and climatic water balance from 1958-2015. Scientific Data 5:170191.

datasets.name: OpenStreetMap basemap
datasets.role: The street map under the habitat maps on this site. Not used in modelling.

software.name: R
software.role: Everything from the pull to the published release.

software.name: rocker/geospatial
software.role: The container image releases are built in, so every map can be rebuilt exactly.

software.name: Node.js and pnpm
software.role: Builds this website.

software.name: Zenodo
software.role: Keeps every archived version of the maps and layers, each with its own DOI, for the life of the repository.

software.name: terra
software.role: Every raster and vector operation: projecting layers onto the grid, terrain, masks, prediction and map drawing.
software.citation: Hijmans RJ. terra: Spatial Data Analysis. R package.

software.name: geodata
software.role: Downloads WorldClim, SoilGrids and WorldCover.

software.name: maxnet
software.role: Fits Maxent, the first of the three models.
software.citation: Phillips SJ, Anderson RP, Dudík M, Schapire RE, Blair ME (2017) Opening the black box: an open-source release of Maxent. Ecography 40:887-893.

software.name: glmnet
software.role: Solves Maxent's penalised fit, called directly so the penalty path can be shorter than maxnet's own, and fits the ridge-penalised regressions that ensembles of small models are made of.
software.citation: Friedman J, Hastie T, Tibshirani R (2010) Regularization paths for generalized linear models via coordinate descent. Journal of Statistical Software 33(1):1-22.

software.name: xgboost
software.role: Fits boosted trees, the second model.
software.citation: Chen T, Guestrin C (2016) XGBoost: a scalable tree boosting system. KDD '16.

software.name: ranger
software.role: Fits the down-sampled random forest, the third model.
software.citation: Wright MN, Ziegler A (2017) ranger: a fast implementation of random forests for high dimensional data in C++ and R. Journal of Statistical Software 77(1).

software.name: blockCV
software.role: Measures how far each taxon's detections are spatially autocorrelated, which sets the block size for cross-validation.
software.citation: Valavi R, Elith J, Lahoz-Monfort JJ, Guillera-Arroita G (2019) blockCV: an R package for generating spatially or environmentally separated folds for k-fold cross-validation of species distribution models. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 10:225-232.

software.name: sf
software.role: Hands survey sites to blockCV as spatial points.
software.citation: Pebesma E (2018) Simple Features for R: standardized support for spatial vector data. The R Journal 10(1):439-446.

software.name: plumber
software.role: Serves the API.

software.name: jsonlite
software.role: Reads and writes every manifest and model record.

software.name: digest
software.role: Record-set fingerprints and content hashes for releases.

software.name: curl
software.role: Asks mycomap.org whether an API token is live, and checks a release image exists before workers pull it.

software.name: openssl
software.role: Checks the Ed25519 signature on a mycomap.org sign-in, and signs Atlas's own session cookie.

software.name: paws.storage
software.role: Publishes and pulls releases through Amazon S3, and signs short-lived download links.

software.name: paws.compute
software.role: Launches and ends the EC2 spot workers that fit models, for the nightly job.

software.name: testthat
software.role: The test suite.

software.name: react
software.role: This website.

software.name: react-dom
software.role: Renders the website in the browser.

software.name: leaflet
software.role: The interactive maps, drawn through a few small React components of Atlas's own.

software.name: @tanstack/react-query
software.role: Fetches and caches API responses.

software.name: wouter
software.role: Page routing.

software.name: lucide-react
software.role: Icons.

software.name: @fontsource-variable/fraunces
software.role: Fraunces, the headings' typeface (Undercase Type), served from this site rather than Google Fonts.

software.name: @fontsource-variable/source-sans-3
software.role: Source Sans 3, the typeface of scientific names (Adobe), served from this site rather than Google Fonts.

software.name: @radix-ui/react-slot
software.role: Button composition, as in shadcn/ui.

software.name: class-variance-authority
software.role: Component variants.

software.name: clsx
software.role: Class names.

software.role: Class names.

software.role: Styling, with mycomap.org's colour tokens.

software.name: tailwindcss-animate
software.role: Styling.

software.name: postcss
software.role: Builds the stylesheet.

software.name: autoprefixer
software.role: Builds the stylesheet.

software.name: vite
software.role: Builds and serves the website.

software.name: @vitejs/plugin-react
software.role: Builds the website.

software.name: typescript
software.role: Type-checks the website.

references.citation: Phillips SJ, Dudík M, Elith J, et al. (2009) Sample selection bias and presence-only distribution models: implications for background and pseudo-absence data. Ecological Applications 19:181-197.
references.used_for: Target-group background: comparing each species with every other validated collection.

references.citation: Elith J, Phillips SJ, Hastie T, et al. (2011) A statistical explanation of MaxEnt for ecologists. Diversity and Distributions 17:43-57.
Valavi R, Elith J, Lahoz-Monfort JJ, Guillera-Arroita G (2021) Modelling species presence-only data with random forests. Ecography 44:1731-1742.

Valavi R, Guillera-Arroita G, Lahoz-Monfort JJ, Elith J (2022) Predictive performance of presence-only species distribution models: a benchmark study with reproducible code. Ecological Monographs 92:e01486.
references.used_for: Choosing the three models and comparing them on the same folds.

references.citation: Roberts DR, Bahn V, Ciuti S, et al. (2017) Cross-validation strategies for data with temporal, spatial, hierarchical, or phylogenetic structure. Ecography 40:913-929.
references.used_for: Scoring on spatial blocks rather than random splits.

references.citation: Hirzel AH, Le Lay G, Helfer V, Randin C, Guisan A (2006) Evaluating the ability of habitat suitability models to predict species presences. Ecological Modelling 199:142-152.
Dormann CF, Elith J, Bacher S, et al. (2013) Collinearity: a review of methods to deal with it and a simulation study evaluating their performance. Ecography 36:27-46.
Warton DI, Renner IW, Ramp D (2013) Model-based control of observer bias for the analysis of presence-only data in ecology. PLoS ONE 8:e79168.
references.used_for: Collecting effort as a predictor, held at one level when a map is drawn.

references.citation: Fithian W, Elith J, Hastie T, Keith DA (2015) Bias correction in species distribution models: pooling survey and collection data for multiple species. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 6:424-438.
references.used_for: Treating other species' collections as the surveys a species could have turned up in.

references.citation: Raes N, ter Steege H (2007) A null-model for significance testing of presence-only species distribution models. Ecography 30:727-736.
references.used_for: Testing every map against null models before it is trusted.

references.citation: Kass JM, Muscarella R, Galante PJ, et al. (2021) ENMeval 2.0: redesigned for customizable and reproducible modeling of species' niches and distributions. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 12:1602-1608.
references.used_for: Tuning Maxent's feature classes and regularisation, and null-model significance, as ENMeval does them.

references.citation: Tedersoo L, Bahram M, Põlme S, et al. (2014) Global diversity and geography of soil fungi. Science 346:1256688.
references.used_for: Soil pH first in Maxent's predictor order.

references.citation: Põlme S, Abarenkov K, Henrik Nilsson R, et al. (2020) FungalTraits: a user-friendly traits database of fungi and fungus-like stramenopiles. Fungal Diversity 105:1-16.
references.used_for: Each taxon's guild, looked up by genus, which decides where the host-tree predictors sit in Maxent's order. Used for lookup only; the table is not redistributed.

products.name: Validated collections, as pulled
products.detail: Every eligible record with its exact coordinates, name and validation state.
products.why: Exact collection points are never published. They stay on mycomap.org and on Atlas's own private compute.

products.name: Collection cells
products.detail: Where each taxon was collected, as 0.1° cells with a record count.

products.name: Taxa by state and province
products.detail: Every taxon in each US state, Canadian province or territory and Mexican state it has been recorded in, with its validated records and independent localities there.

products.name: Taxon counts and fingerprints
products.detail: Records, independent localities and the record-set hash for each of the 17,000+ taxa.

products.name: Raw environmental downloads
products.detail: WorldClim, SoilGrids and WorldCover exactly as downloaded, about 15 GB, and the BIGMAP and NFI tree-species layers the host-tree predictors are built from.
products.why: Get them from the providers linked above; Atlas does not re-host another project's data.

products.name: Predictor stack on the Atlas grid
products.detail: All 53 predictors reprojected to North America Albers: 5 km (about 100 MB) and 1 km (about 2.2 GB) GeoTIFFs, with a manifest of their checksums.
products.why: Archived on Zenodo as the layers series, a new version with its own DOI whenever a layer is rebuilt. The first version is waiting to be published; it will appear under Downloads. The stack carries WorldClim's ShareAlike licence.

products.name: Fungal guild per genus
products.detail: The FungalTraits primary lifestyle of each genus, which orders Maxent's predictors.
products.why: FungalTraits' licence does not clearly allow redistribution, so Atlas only looks genera up in it. Get the table from its authors (Põlme et al. 2020). Each model's guild is recorded with its scores.

products.name: Training tables
products.detail: For each taxon, its presence cells and background cells with the value of every predictor, and the spatial fold each row was scored in.
products.why: A table with cell positions would publish presence cells at 5 km or 1 km. The plan is to release them with positions removed: enough to refit every model exactly.

products.name: Predictors chosen per taxon
products.detail: Which predictors survived correlation pruning and the one-per-four cap.

products.name: Scores on every spatial fold
products.detail: AUC and Boyce on each held-out block, for each of the three models.

products.name: Fitted model objects
products.detail: The fitted Maxent, boosted-tree and forest objects, to predict with on other layers.
products.why: Not stored yet: a fit keeps its scores and map and discards the object.

products.name: Suitability rasters
products.detail: Each model's raw suitability as a GeoTIFF on the Atlas grid, inside the 500 km accessible area.
products.where: /api/taxa/{name}/raster.tif, for anyone signed in with a mycomap.org account or holding a token. Releases chosen for archiving go to Zenodo as the models series, each version with its own DOI (see Downloads).

products.name: Rank maps
products.detail: The coloured maps on this site: each cell's percentile within its own map.

products.name: Benchmarks and sweeps
products.detail: The three models scored on the same folds, and the predictor-cap sweep.
products.where: /api/benchmarks/latest (the newest benchmark). Earlier benchmarks and sweeps are summarised in the repository README.

products.name: Release manifests
products.detail: Every published file with its SHA-256, plus the code commit, package versions, layer builds and pull fingerprint.
products.why: Written with every release, and included as release.json in each Zenodo models version.

products.name: Where each species is likely, by state and province
products.detail: Each map counted by state when it is drawn: the cells within reach, and the cells it rates at least as highly as the poorer tenth of the places the species was found. Over the maps that beat their null models, a state is likely when that covers a tenth of it on average, and possible when it does on one map only.
products.where: /api/taxa/{name}/regions, /api/checklist.csv, and the regions field of every model's metrics

products.name: Map pictures
products.detail: A taxon's map drawn over Natural Earth land and borders with its collections, a legend and the source, for spreadsheets, documents and slides.
